title: Carrying a Revised Pledge Up to a Round Lot
content:
Receipts over grain held under Grain Storage and Conditioning Agreements are written in round lots, so the revised pledge is carried up rather than left ragged. How far it is carried turns on how many receipts have been issued against the agreement over the last twelve months.

## What the tariff lays down

Where more than one receipt has been issued against the agreement in the last twelve months, the revised pledge is carried up to the next whole thousand bushels.

Where one receipt has been issued against the agreement in the last twelve months, it is carried up to the next whole hundred bushels.

And otherwise it stands as it was worked out.

## The bands set out

| Receipts issued against the agreement in the last twelve months | The revised pledge |
| --- | --- |
| more than one | carried up to the next whole thousand bushels |
| exactly one | carried up to the next whole hundred bushels |
| none | stands as it was worked out |

Carrying up is always upward: a figure already standing on a whole thousand is left as it is under the first line, and a figure already standing on a whole hundred is left as it is under the second.

## Worked roundings, on a hypothetical figure

Take a revised pledge worked out at 13240.75 bushels.

**Three receipts issued over the last twelve months.** Carried up to the next whole thousand, the pledge stands at 14000.

**One receipt issued over the last twelve months.** Carried up to the next whole hundred, the pledge stands at 13300.

**No receipt issued over the last twelve months.** The pledge stands at 13240.75 as it was worked out.

## A figure already on a round lot

A revised pledge worked out at exactly 9000 bushels with three receipts over the twelve months stands at 9000, already being a whole thousand; with one receipt over the twelve months it likewise stands at 9000, already being a whole hundred.
